create.name: Akincano Marc Weber
create.bio:
Akincano Marc Weber is a Swiss-born Buddhist teacher who lives in the Rhineland and teaches from Cologne. Drawn to meditation as a teenager, he sat first in Soto Zen settings before ordaining in the mid-1980s as a bhikkhu at Chithurst in England, in the Thai forest lineage of Ajahn Chah under Ajahn Sumedho. He spent some twenty years as a monk in Britain, Thailand and Switzerland, including several years studying Pali and the suttas with Bhikkhu Payutto, and returned to lay life in 2005. He later trained in Core Process Psychotherapy at the Karuna Institute and holds an MA in mindfulness-based psychotherapy practice.

His teaching stays close to the early discourses, read before they hardened into schools and commentaries, and he describes himself as belonging to no single lineage today. Typical themes are satipaṭṭhāna, breath meditation, calm and insight, the brahmavihāras and the psychology of contemplative life. He co-founded Bodhi College in 2015 and teaches its European courses, guides Atammaya, a Cologne community with a weekly online evening offered on donation, and leads retreats and study programmes in Europe and the United States, including at the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies. More than three hundred of his talks are free on Dharma Seed.

courses.title: The Thermals of Awakening
courses.description: A two-week residential Bodhi College course co-led with Ajahn Sucitto at ITC Naarden in the Netherlands. It follows the Buddha's gradual path as a natural, unfolding process, with sitting practice, talks and reflection.

courses.title: In the Buddha's Presence: Individuality and Liberation
courses.description: A four-night study retreat at the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies in Massachusetts that looks at the early Buddhist texts through the lives of the Buddha's disciples and how each was taught according to temperament. Days combine study sessions, group work and silent sitting.

courses.title: Making the Most of Suffering: Stories of Failing Forward
courses.description: A hybrid study retreat with the scholar Andy Rotman, run by BCBS with Bodhi College, that reads Pali and Sanskrit stories and Buddhist art about meeting dukkha with courage and skill. It can be joined in residence or online.

courses.title: Atammaya Online Meditation Evening
courses.description: A two-hour Wednesday evening on Zoom, taught in German, with a short instruction, silent sitting, a Dharma talk and time for questions. It runs on a donation basis and the link is sent through his newsletter.

free_resources.title: Four dimensions of contemplative practice
free_resources.description: A 2026 talk recorded at the Insight Meditation Society on four ways of understanding what we are doing when we meditate. Free to stream or download on Dharma Seed.

free_resources.title: Guided Mettā Meditation (no phrases)
free_resources.description: A guided loving-kindness practice that works without the usual repeated phrases, resting instead on felt warmth and intention. Free on Dharma Seed.

free_resources.title: Akincano Marc Weber's talks on Dharma Seed
free_resources.description: His full archive of more than three hundred recorded talks and guided meditations from retreats in Europe and the United States, in English, German and French.
